# Reading GAP-04: Residues not compared are classed in this order: microheterogeneity, UNK, pairing disagrees, insertion code, Not_Observed in SIFTS, SIFTS anomaly (GAP-07); then R10 with R6 as clarified ('outside' only when neither path gives a position and n is below 1 or above the reference's length).
# Reading GAP-05: An insertion-code residue (R5) is counted under 'insertion code' (K9), its two paths reported, and it is not joined. No modelled residue in the 26 carries one.

# Reading GAP-06: The pairing check (R3 amended) requires _pdbx_poly_seq_scheme's pdb_seq_num and auth_seq_num, pdb_ins_code and pdb_strand_id at the residue's label_asym_id and label_seq_id to equal the atom records'; a residue whose atoms carry two label_seq_ids 'pairing disagrees'. Seen before the run (the mmCIFs only): auth_seq_num equals pdb_seq_num at every modelled RyR1 residue of the 26, so requiring both makes no difference there.

# Reading GAP-07: Criteria 2.2: in a chain SIFTS maps, a modelled residue whose chain and number SIFTS does not list at all, or to which SIFTS gives more than one UniProt position or a cross-reference without a position, is a 'SIFTS anomaly': reported, not joined, counted in K9. Only a residue SIFTS lists with no UniProt cross-reference of its own is 'path A only (residue)' (R8 and R10 amended), joined on m_A, marked.
# Reading GAP-08: 'Another accession' with m_A a gap or ambiguous is 'neither path' (R10 amended names only 'none').
# Reading GAP-09: R8's stop on another accession fires if any residue SIFTS lists for a RyR1 chain carries a UniProt cross-reference to an accession other than the reference or its '-1'.

# Reading GAP-10: A declaration (R10 amended) is a _struct_ref_seq_dif row of the residue's entity (through align_id) and chain (pdbx_pdb_strand_id) whose seq_num is the residue's label_seq_id. Seen before the run (the mmCIFs only): every declaration on a RyR1 entity of the 26 is made for every chain of its entity, so this gives the same result as the criteria's 'that entity and residue'.

# Reading GAP-11: R11: residues not compared (UNK, microheterogeneity, pairing disagrees, insertion code, Not_Observed in SIFTS, SIFTS anomaly, outside) form runs of their own class, grouped by class alone, and so break runs of compared residues; undeclared differences stay in their run (version 2.1). Seen before the run: the pre-check (the mmCIFs only) found no UNK, microheterogeneity, insertion code or residue with two label_seq_ids in author 2740-2930 of any RyR1 chain of the five departing pig entries; the critique of criteria 2.2, emulating path S by path A, found no pairing disagreement in the 26 and the run unbroken at 2736-2939 in all 20 chains. So this reading cannot decide K8.
# Reading GAP-12: R12 'equal': residues on path S only or neither path do not prevent it (they are listed and not joined); a chain with no residue at a species position is 'nothing compared'.
# Reading GAP-13: R12 'departs': a run of status agree, or path A only, whose offset is not 0, identity-low or not (an identity-low run is also 'disputed').
# Reading GAP-14: R11: a run with no counted residue (only declared differences) has no identity and is not 'identity low'.

# Reading GAP-15: R13 describes the boundary with the run before the departing segment only. 'Unmodelled' at the boundary: deposited residues between the two (label_seq_id gap) or reference residues absent between them (path A's deletion columns), or (criteria 2.2) reference residues absent just after the run's last residue, where path A can slide a residue across an omitted stretch; 'next to UNK': the run before is UNK. A determinable boundary where both tests fire is described as 'both'.

# Reading GAP-16: Criteria 2.2: K4-P renumbers the whole mmCIF in memory (the atom records and _pdbx_poly_seq_scheme's pdb_seq_num and auth_seq_num), not SIFTS, so only path S's comparison can catch it; K4b-P renumbers the same ranges in the atom records and SIFTS's PDB cross-references, not _pdbx_poly_seq_scheme, so only the pairing check (R3 amended) can catch it. Both are judged per residue.
# Reading GAP-17: K7-P passes when each planted residue ends not joined (version 2.1); whether each is 'disputed' (version 2) is reported beside it.
# Reading GAP-18: K8: a chain passes if a run of status agree or path A only with m_A - n = +1 lies within 2700-2960 and covers 2740-2930; a run covering 2740-2930 with another offset fails it.
# Reading GAP-19: K5-P's 'mismatches': residues at a species position (paths agree, or path A only) whose type differs from the reference there, declared or not.
# Reading GAP-20: A residue type outside the twenty standard ones (none in the 26's RyR1 entities) is typed by its comp id and so always differs from the reference.
# Reading GAP-21: R14 reads the gate residue at S13's author number with no insertion code; R15 compares O2's reads at the species position (O2 read at the UniProt position).
# Reading GAP-22: UNK residues are listed in the exceptions table as runs (R4: chain and author range), with the count SIFTS gives a position for.
# Reading GAP-23: Exactly one retrieval record must name each input; more than one is refused.
# Reading GAP-24: The tables say no outcome may be used if K9 fails, as they do when a planted fault is missed or K8 fails (both of which the criteria name).
# Reading GAP-25: The run guard requires every file in DEPENDS to be committed, retrieval.jsonl included, so the SIFTS fetch's records are committed before the run (as S13's guard required).
# Reading GAP-26: SIFTS unreachable for every entry stops the run (R8 amended), where 'How each outcome is read' had the run go on path A alone; version 2 holds where it differs.

# Reading GAP-27: Criteria 2.2: the tables' column names are lower case (path_s, offset_a, m_s, unk and so on), an empty cell means no value, and a flag is true or false, as the graph's tables are written (the schema's column-name pattern and validator rule V09). The comment lines above the column line, and the tables' place under curation/, are left to the recording of each table in the graph.

# Reading GAP-28: Criteria 2.2: a planted fault judged per residue (K4-P, K4b-P, K7-P, K11-P) tests something only if more than half of its residues were joined in the real run; otherwise it is not caught.
# Reading GAP-29: Criteria 2.2: each run writes its three tables to curation/cl2_run_<the commit's first seven characters>/, so a repeat run never needs an earlier run's record removed.
